key_insight: The paper turns relativistic hydrodynamics admissibility constraints into a solvable linear-inequality limiter, enabling high-order finite-difference schemes to stay physical without iterative tuning.
engineering_relevance: This gives CFD practitioners a practical way to prevent negative density/pressure and superluminal states in extreme-flow simulations while preserving sharp shocks and high-order accuracy.
method: Use a GQL reformulation to express relativistic physical constraints as linear inequalities.
Embed a Zalesak-style FCT flux limiter directly in conservative variables for finite-difference WENO.
Compute optimal limiter parameters non-iteratively via stereographic parameterization and small symmetric eigenproblems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports extensive tests from 1D to 3D, including ultra-relativistic Riemann problems and astrophysical jets, showing robust admissibility enforcement and design-order accuracy on smooth cases.
watch_item: The multidimensional relaxed variants reduce cost, but the eigenproblem-based limiter still adds implementation complexity and overhead compared with standard high-order finite-difference schemes.
paper_title: GQL-Based Physical-Constraint-Preserving High-Order Finite Difference Schemes for Special Relativistic Hydrodynamics in Arbitrary Dimensions
